editorial.titleTr: Presidential Candidate's Identity Leaked After Discussing First-Generation Aircraft Seat Replacement
summaryTr: Personal information of 168 passengers aboard Air Force One, including President Lee Jae-myung and his spouse, leaked for five months
Personal data suspected to have been exposed externally during malware scanning of Europe trip files
Joint investigation by Foreign Ministry, Presidential Office, and police underscores need for comprehensive government security overhaul
editorial.bodyTr: The personal information of 168 passengers aboard Air Force One, including President Lee Jae-myung and his spouse, was exposed on overseas websites for approximately five months starting June 2, 2026. The personal data of the passengers is suspected to have been leaked externally during the government's process of conducting malware scans on files related to a European visit. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Blue House, and police are investigating the circumstances of the leak and whether it was further distributed, while the need for a comprehensive overhaul of the security system has grown.

editorials.titleTr: House Prices Up 90 Weeks, But President Says They're Falling "Dramatically
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung claims house prices are falling at a 'remarkable' rate
In reality, Seoul apartments have risen for 90 consecutive weeks, with declines limited to parts of Gangnam
Gap between government claims and statistical data prompts calls for objective explanation
editorials.bodyTr: President Lee Jae-myung stated during a cabinet meeting on November 3rd that transaction prices in major regions are falling dramatically. According to statistics from Korea Real Estate Board, Seoul apartment prices have risen for 90 consecutive weeks through the fourth week of October, with declines appearing only in parts of Gangnam. The editorial points out that private statistics also show no clear signs of sharp decline, emphasizing that the government must accurately explain objective data to the public.

editorials.titleTr: Marathon Gridlock Paralyzes Seoul Every Weekend—Something Has to Give
summaryTr: Seoul's downtown marathons cause weekly traffic paralysis.
Marathon events nationwide surge to 610, with 181 in Seoul.
City lacks direct control structure; improving management system is urgent.
editorials.bodyTr: A large-scale marathon held in downtown Seoul on the first caused severe traffic congestion due to major road closures. As the running craze has grown, marathon events have proliferated, with projections showing 610 events nationwide and 181 in Seoul by 2026. Given the structural difficulty for the Seoul city government to directly regulate marathons, there is a need to review dedicated management systems and examine how costs are being shouldered.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Does the President Who Promised to Care for the Underprivileged Only See Gangnam Housing Prices Falling?
summaryTr: The president cited only the decline in Gangnam housing prices while insisting on market stability.
Ordinary residents in the northern Seoul area are suffering from soaring housing prices and rents.
Policy changes are more urgent than government report distortions and loan restrictions.
editorial.bodyTr: The president cited falling property prices in certain areas like Gangnam in Seoul to claim market stabilization, yet ordinary citizens living in areas north of the Han River are suffering from soaring housing prices and rents. Critics argue that the government's lending restrictions and inaccurate reports are distorting market realities, and that policy changes rather than mobilizing investigative agencies are urgently needed.

summaryTr: Personal information of 168 members of an overseas delegation was exposed for five months.
The government belatedly moved to reissue passports.
Urgent need for fundamental preventive measures to overhaul public institution security systems.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: President Says "Housing Prices in Major Areas Are Falling at an Astonishing Rate
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung raised concerns about the credibility of real estate statistics by citing a sharp decline in Gangnam apartment prices.
In reality, Seoul apartment prices overall have been rising for 90 consecutive weeks, with non-Gangnam areas remaining strong.
An approach that dismisses statistics wholesale only erodes government credibility and lacks substantive alternatives.
editorial.bodyTr:
President Lee Jae-myung stated at a cabinet meeting yesterday that apartment listings in the Seoul area are rapidly increasing and transaction volumes are quickly declining, with actual transaction prices in major areas falling at a remarkable rate. He also expressed concern that "real estate-related statistics may not be properly conveyed to the public," and diagnosed that "there are aspects where those who stand to benefit from rising housing prices are selectively using some of that data and pushing it in one direction."

It is true that apartment price declines have accelerated recently in Gangnam's three districts (Seocho, Gangnam, and Songpa), which are densely populated with high-end apartments. Statistics from the Korea Real Estate Board last week also showed pronounced downward trends in the three Gangnam districts. Media reports have emerged that actual transaction prices for Gangnam redevelopment apartments have fallen by hundreds of millions to tens of billions of won. However, it is an undeniable fact that according to Korea Real Estate Board statistics, apartment prices in Seoul overall have risen for 90 consecutive weeks. While the rate of increase has diminished significantly, non-Gangnam areas such as Seongbuk and Seodaemun districts remain strong, and all 22 other districts in Seoul excluding the three Gangnam districts have risen. Particularly as jeonse and monthly rent increases show no signs of moderating, housing insecurity among ordinary citizens is intensifying. Sharp reactions from opposition parties to the president's real estate remarks were understandable, such as "it seems they're trying to fix the statistics since they can't control housing prices."

The controversy surrounding the accuracy of weekly apartment price statistics is nothing new. In the previous administration, then-Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport Won Hee-ryong expressed similar concerns about weekly statistics. Efforts to produce more accurate housing price statistics must continue. However, discrediting existing statistics outright without offering proper alternatives, or claiming that those profiting from housing price increases are skewing statistics one way, causes only confusion and undermines the credibility of government diagnoses. Ultimately, housing price stability cannot be achieved without supply policies that earn market trust and market-friendly measures. There can be no disagreement with President Lee's point that for the future of the Republic of Korea, we must move away from being a real estate speculation republic. However, it is unfortunate to watch the president argue that the housing market is stabilizing based on apartment price declines in some areas, much like an endless Native American rain dance continuing until rain actually falls.

editorials.body: 입력 업데이트 종합 26면 더불어민주당 김민석 대표가 어제 비공개 의원총회에서 “반명·분열주의·신천지 3자 비밀연합의 근거를 못 찾았다. 피해를 보신 분들께 죄송하다”는 취지로 말했다고 김성회 민주당 원내 대변인이 전했다. 이날 예정된 신천지 의혹에 대한 당 TF의 보고는 취소됐고, 대신 김 대표의 사과가 있었다고 한다. 신천지 의혹은 지난 8월 민주당 전당대회 기간에 친명(이재명)계와 친청(정청래)계로 당을 갈라지게 하고, 지금도 계파 갈등의 빌미가 되고 있는 사안이다. 최초로 의혹을 제기한 김 대표는 전당대회 승리 이후에도 “상당한 정도의 집단적 가입이 있었다”고 말해 왔는데 지금 와서 갑자기 발을 빼는 듯한 모습을 보인 것이다. 당원과 국민의 우려는 안중에도 없는 무책임한 자세를 집권여당 대표가 보인 게 놀라울 따름이다. 김민석 더불어민주당 대표가 3일 오후 서울 여의도 국회에서 열린 의원총회에서 생각에 잠겨 있다. 뉴스1 전당대회 때 신천지를 둘러싸고 민주당에서 벌어진 상황을 복기해 보면 국민의 당혹감은 더 커지게 된다. 김 대표는 “반명·분열주의·신천지 3자 비밀연합을 깨는 것이 이번 전대의 본질”이라며 친청계를 압박했다. 친청계와 신천지의 유착을 의심케 하는 공세에 친청계는 지금도 “의혹의 근거를 대라”며 반발하고 있다. 어제의 사과는 마타도어로 당선되고 뒤늦게 말을 바꾸는 몰염치이거나 자기 주장의 앞뒤가 맞지 않는 자가당착이다. 정청래 전 대표는 어제 “당원들에게 모욕감과 혼란을 주고 당을 위험에 빠뜨린 행위에 대해 어떤 책임을 질 것인지 공개적으로 밝혀주시길 바란다”고 했다. 정치와 종교의 야합은 이재명 대통령도 강하게 비판해 왔다. “정교분리 원칙은 중요한 헌법적 결단이며 이를 어기는 행위는 헌법과 헌정 질서를 훼손하는 중대한 사안”이라고 했다. 통일교와 신천지에 연루 의혹이 먼저 제기된 국민의힘을 겨냥한 발언이었지만, 민주당에도 똑같이 적용돼야 한다. 국민은 여야를 막론하고 정교유착 비리를 명백하게 밝혀 잘못에 상응하는 책임을 지우길 원한다. 김 대표의 사과가 진심이라면 TF가 파악한 진상을 투명하게 공개하고, 파악된 진상이 미진하다면 수사를 통해서라도 진실을 밝혀내야 한다. 당리당략과 계파 유불리를 계산한 사과는 국민의 공감을 얻을 수 없다. 무책임한 의혹 제기였다면 사과보다 국민을 우롱한 책임을 지는 게 먼저다.

summary: 민주당 김민석 대표가 신천지 의혹 근거 불찾았다며 사과로 입장 변경.

editorials.titleTr: [Editorial] Ruling Party Leader's Shifting Story on Shincheonji Suspicions—Is This Really a 'Never Mind' Matter?
summaryTr: Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok apologized and changed his stance after failing to find evidence of Shincheonji allegations.
Withdrawing allegations that were strongly raised during the party convention immediately after taking office is irresponsible.
The public is urging both ruling and opposition parties to investigate and hold accountable for collusion between politics and religion.
editorials.bodyTr:
Democratic Party Chairman Kim Min-seok said at a closed caucus yesterday that he "could not find evidence of a secret alliance between anti-Lee forces, factionalists, and Shincheonji," and apologized to those who suffered harm, according to Democratic Party spokesperson Kim Sung-hoe. The party's task force report on Shincheonji suspicions, which was scheduled for that day, was canceled, and instead there was an apology from Chairman Kim. The Shincheonji allegations emerged during the Democratic Party's national convention in August, dividing the party between the pro-Lee Jae-myung and pro-Jung Chul-gun factions, and continue to fuel factional conflict. Chairman Kim, who initially raised the allegations, continued to say even after winning the convention that "there was a considerable degree of collective recruitment," but now appears to be backing away abruptly. It is remarkable that the ruling party's chairman has shown such irresponsibility, with no regard for party members' and the public's concerns.

During the national convention, reviewing what happened in the Democratic Party surrounding Shincheonji only deepens public bewilderment. Chairman Kim pressured the pro-Jung faction by saying "breaking the secret alliance between anti-Lee forces, factionalists, and Shincheonji is the essence of this convention." In response to accusations suggesting collusion between the pro-Jung faction and Shincheonji, the pro-Jung faction continues to counter by saying "provide evidence of the allegations." Yesterday's apology is either shamelessness of using a matador tactic and changing one's tune belatedly, or self-contradiction where one's argument lacks internal consistency. Former Chairman Jung Chul-gun said yesterday, "I hope you will publicly clarify what responsibility you will take for actions that have brought insult and confusion to party members and put the party in danger." The collusion between politics and religion has been strongly criticized by President Lee Jae-myung. He said, "The principle of separation of church and state is an important constitutional decision, and violating it is a grave matter that undermines the constitutional and constitutional order." This was directed at the People Power Party, which first faced allegations of involvement with the Unification Church and Shincheonji, but it must apply equally to the Democratic Party. The public wants both ruling and opposition parties to clearly expose collusion between politics and religion and hold those responsible proportional to their wrongdoings. If Chairman Kim's apology is sincere, he must transparently disclose the truth identified by the task force, and if the identified truth is incomplete, the truth must be revealed through investigation. An apology calculated on party interests and factional advantage cannot win public sympathy. If the suspicions were irresponsible allegations, taking responsibility for ridiculing the public should come before an apology.

editorials.title: [사설] 북한에 태권도 유네스코 등재 선수 뺏긴 한심한 문화외교
editorials.body: 입력 업데이트 종합 26면 대한민국의 국기 태권도가 유네스코 인류무형문화유산 등재에서 북한에 선수를 빼앗길 처지다. 허민 국가유산청장은 2일 북한이 신청한 ‘조선민주주의인민공화국의 전통무술-태권도’에 ‘등재 권고’가 예상된다며, 남북 공동 등재에 힘썼으나 현 시점에서 사실상 어렵다고 밝혔다. 태권도를 세계에 보급한 종주국이면서 정작 인류문화유산 등재는 북한에 밀린 일이 그저 청장이 SNS에 “안타깝게 생각한다” 정도로 표명할 일인가. 사안의 심각성을 인식하지 못하는 안일한 모습이다. 이번 정부만의 책임은 아니다. 북한은 2024년 3월 단독 등재를 신청했지만 윤석열 정부는 별다른 대응을 하지 않았다. 이재명 정부 들어 올해 3월 말에야 단독 등재 신청서를 냈다. 앞서 박근혜 정부는 2016년 등재를 추진했으나 결실을 보지 못했다. 문재인 정부 시기인 2018년 남북 태권도 단체가 공동 등재에 합의했으나 신청으로 이어지지 않았다. 신청에 앞서 필요하다고 여겨진 태권도의 국가무형문화유산 지정이 역사성과 고유성에 대한 학계의 논란으로 보류됐기 때문이다. 그 사이 남북관계는 경색됐다. 이재명 대통령과 레젭 타입 에르도안 튀르키예 대통령이 3일 청와대에서 열린 공식환영식에서 육군 태권도 시범대의 특별 공연을 지켜보고 있다. 청와대사진기자단 문제는 우리가 태권도의 올림픽 종목화와 해외 보급에 도취해 문화유산으로서의 정체성을 정리하고 세계에 공식화하는 데 소홀했다는 점이다. 정부는 2018년 씨름의 남북 공동 등재 성공에 기대어 태권도도 같은 방식으로 추진하려 했다. 그러나 북한이 2023년 말 ‘적대적 두 국가’를 천명한 후 단독 등재 신청까지 했는데도 독자 등재에 신속히 나서지 않고 방관했다. 전략적 판단 부재가 아닐 수 없다. 유네스코 선등재가 독점권을 뜻하지는 않는다. 예컨대 아리랑은 한국이 2012년 먼저 등재한 뒤, 북한이 2014년 별도 등재했다. 한국의 태권도도 별도 등재될 수 있다. 그렇다고 해서 정부의 한심한 문화외교가 면죄부를 받을 수 있는 것은 아니다. 북한의 최종 등재 여부는 12월 중국 샤먼 유네스코 위원회에서 결정된다. 앞으로 정부는 외교력을 총동원해 한국 태권도의 역사와 전승 실태를 국제사회에 알리고, 유네스코 등재의 남은 가능성을 치밀하게 두드려야 할 것이다.

역대 정부의 전략 부재와 미흡한 대응이 현 사태를 초래했다.

editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Korea's Shameful Cultural Diplomacy Loses Taekwondo UNESCO-Listed Athletes to North Korea
summaryTr: North Korea applied first to have taekwondo registered with UNESCO, leaving South Korea at risk of falling behind.
The absence of strategy and inadequate responses from successive governments have led to the current situation.
The government must mobilize all diplomatic resources to pursue separate registration of Korean taekwondo.
editorials.bodyTr: South Korea's taekwondo, the nation's iconic martial art, stands to lose to North Korea in the race for UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage status. On the 2nd, Heo Min, commissioner of the Cultural Heritage Administration, stated that North Korea's application for "Traditional Martial Arts of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea—Taekwondo" is expected to receive a "recommendation for inscription." He noted that while the government made efforts toward joint North-South listing, it is now practically difficult at this point. As the birthplace and global advocate of taekwondo, should South Korea's loss in UNESCO heritage designation to North Korea simply be expressed by the commissioner as "regrettable" on social media? This reveals a complacent failure to grasp the gravity of the situation. The responsibility does not lie solely with the current administration. Although North Korea submitted its application for sole listing in March 2024, the Yoon Suk Yeol government took no particular action in response. It was not until late March of this year, under the Lee Jae-myung administration, that a sole application was filed. Previously, the Park Geun-hye government pursued inscription in 2016 but failed to achieve results. During the Moon Jae-in administration in 2018, North and South Korean taekwondo organizations agreed on joint listing, but this did not lead to an application. The designation of taekwondo as a national intangible cultural asset, considered necessary before applying, was held up due to academic controversy over its historicity and uniqueness. Meanwhile, inter-Korean relations grew tense. The problem is that we became absorbed in making taekwondo an Olympic sport and promoting it overseas, neglecting to clarify its identity as a cultural heritage and formalize it internationally. The government had hoped to promote taekwondo through joint listing with North Korea following the successful 2018 co-registration of ssirum. However, even after North Korea declared itself an "adversarial two-state system" in late 2023 and subsequently submitted its own application, the government neither promptly pursued independent listing nor took decisive action. This represents nothing short of an absence of strategic judgment. UNESCO listing does not confer exclusive rights. For example, Arirang was first registered by South Korea in 2012, and then North Korea separately registered it in 2014. South Korean taekwondo can likewise be listed separately. Nevertheless, this cannot absolve the government of its shameful cultural diplomacy. North Korea's final inscription will be decided in December at the UNESCO committee meeting in Xiamen, China. Going forward, the government must mobilize all its diplomatic resources to introduce the history and transmission practices of Korean taekwondo to the international community and carefully pursue remaining possibilities for UNESCO listing.

editorial.title: Rebalancing support
editorial.body: Korea needs targeted family support and a long-term immigration policy Welfare policy can turn a narrow question of eligibility into a national argument about belonging. A case in point is South Korea’s debate over multicultural family support, which began with complaints about priority access to subsidized postpartum care. It now tests whether outdated rules can be corrected without casting suspicion on those they were meant to help. The trigger was an online post asking why mothers from multicultural families shared a second-priority category with women in the national merit category when booking places through Seoul’s subsidized postpartum care program. President Lee Jae Myung took up the complaint on X, arguing that welfare should reflect financial need rather than cultural background. He has also said that programs addressing language and cultural barriers should continue. A review of current rules is justified. The Ministry of Justice has asked local governments to examine support programs and related ordinances. Seoul has begun inspecting 26 programs. Other ministries have signaled reviews. The findings should be made public, including who has received each benefit and whether families in greater need have been denied access. Korea’s multicultural policies took shape in 2006, as international marriages, particularly in rural areas, brought the hardships faced by marriage migrants and their children into public view. Support later extended to childcare and housing. The original case for assistance was clear: Many families faced poverty or language barriers and struggled to settle into Korean society. Households covered by those policies now span a wider range of economic circumstances. The share of multicultural households with monthly income above 6 million won ($4,480) rose from 2.9 percent in 2015 to 10.4 percent in 2024, according to survey data. The figures do not show that most are affluent. They do show that family background alone says little about a household’s ability to pay. That distinction matters when family status itself confers priority. It is hard to defend giving a well-off household precedence over a low-income Korean family seeking the same limited service. A migrant mother, however, may have few relatives nearby to help after childbirth, a circumstance income figures cannot capture. An effective review would trace each benefit to the disadvantage it is meant to offset and test whether its eligibility rules reach the households that need it. Where poverty is the concern, income and assets should matter more than family category. Where language barriers are at issue, tailored services may remain justified. That scrutiny should remain directed at the policies themselves. Immigrants as a group should not be made answerable for flaws in individual programs. A survey cited in the debate found that 13 percent of multicultural families had experienced discrimination. Their net enrollment rate in higher education was 61.9 percent, 13 percentage points below the national average. Criticism of poorly designed benefits can become a pretext for disparaging people who still face substantial obstacles. The definition of a multicultural family also leaves some immigrant households outside the framework. Programs largely focus on households formed by a Korean national and a foreign spouse, excluding families in which both parents are foreign nationals. Foreign workers, too, are part of Korea’s response to a shrinking workforce. Policy built around one family category cannot serve as an immigration strategy. The national population strategy released last month gave little attention to multicultural households and foreign workers. A dedicated immigration agency, discussed under the previous administration but never established, could coordinate integration policy with education and employment policy. Benefit-by-benefit revisions cannot tell the country how it will sustain its workforce, as births remain low. Clear criteria can make a postpartum-care queue fair. How Korea incorporates newcomers will shape its demographic future, far beyond the next place in line. editorial.bodyTr: 한국은 표적화된 가족 지원과 장기적 이민 정책이 필요하다. 복지 정책은 좁은 적격성 문제를 국가의 소속감에 관한 논쟁으로 바꿀 수 있다. 한국의 다문화 가족 지원을 둘러싼 논쟁이 바로 그 사례다. 이 논쟁은 보조 출산 후 관리에 우선 접근권을 놓고 불만으로 시작됐다. 이제는 구식 규칙을 시정할 때 그 규칙이 도움을 주려던 사람들에게 의심을 품지 않을 수 있는지를 시험하고 있다. 촉발제는 서울의 보조 출산 후 관리 프로그램을 통해 예약할 때 다문화 가족의 어머니들이 국가 공로 범주의 여성들과 함께 2순위 범주에 있는 이유를 묻는 온라인 게시물이었다. 이준석 대통령이 X에서 이 불만을 제기하며 복지는 문화적 배경이 아닌 경제적 필요를 반영해야 한다고 주장했다. 그는 또한 언어 및 문화적 장벽을 다루는 프로그램은 계속되어야 한다고 말했다. 현 규칙을 검토하는 것은 정당하다. 법무부는 지방자치단체에 지원 프로그램과 관련 조례를 검토하도록 요청했다. 서울은 26개 프로그램을 검사하기 시작했다. 다른 부처들도 검토를 시사했다. 조사 결과는 누가 각 혜택을 받았는지, 더 큰 필요가 있는 가족들이 접근이 거부됐는지 포함하여 공개되어야 한다. 한국의 다문화 정책은 2006년에 국제결혼, 특히 농촌 지역에서 결혼 이주자들과 그들의 자녀들이 직면한 어려움이 공론화되면서 형성되었다. 지원은 나중에 보육과 주택으로 확대됐다. 지원의 원래 근거는 명확했다. 많은 가족들이 빈곤이나 언어 장벽에 직면했고 한국 사회 정착에 어려움을 겪었다. 현재 이 정책들이 포괄하는 가정들은 경제적 상황이 더욱 다양해졌다. 월 소득이 600만 원 이상인 다문화 가구의 비중은 2015년 2.9퍼센트에서 2024년 10.4퍼센트로 증가했다. 이 수치들이 대부분이 부유하다는 것을 보여주지는 않는다. 가족 배경만으로는 가구의 납부 능력에 대해 거의 말해주지 못한다는 것을 보여준다. 가족 신분 자체가 우선권을 부여할 때 그 구분은 중요하다. 같은 제한된 서비스를 찾는 저소득 한국 가족보다 부유한 가구에 우선권을 주는 것은 방어하기 어렵다. 그러나 이주 어머니는 출산 후 도움을 줄 친척이 근처에 거의 없을 수 있으며, 이는 소득 수치가 포착할 수 없는 상황이다. 효과적인 검토는 각 혜택을 그것이 상쇄하려는 불리한 상황으로 추적하고 그 적격성 규칙이 필요한 가구에 도달하는지 테스트할 것이다. 빈곤이 문제인 곳에서는 소득과 자산이 가족 범주보다 더 중요해야 한다. 언어 장벽이 문제인 곳에서는 맞춤형 서비스가 정당할 수 있다. 그 정밀 검사는 정책 자체에 지향되어야 한다. 이민자 집단은 개별 프로그램의 결함에 대해 책임을 져야 하지 않는다. 논쟁에서 인용된 설문조사에 따르면 다문화 가족의 13퍼센트가 차별을 경험했다. 그들의 고등교육 순 진학률은 61.9퍼센트로 전국 평균보다 13 포인트 낮았다. 설계가 부실한 혜택에 대한 비판은 여전히 상당한 장애물에 직면한 사람들을 폄하하는 구실이 될 수 있다. 다문화 가족의 정의도 일부 이민자 가구를 체계 밖으로 남긴다. 프로그램은 주로 한국 국민과 외국 배우자로 이루어진 가구에 초점을 맞추며 양쪽 부모 모두 외국인인 가족을 제외한다. 외국 노동자 역시 감소하는 인력에 대한 한국의 대응의 일부다. 한 가족 범주를 중심으로 구축된 정책은 이민 전략으로 기능할 수 없다. 지난달 발표된 국가 인구 전략은 다문화 가구와 외국 노동자에 거의 주의를 기울이지 않았다. 이전 행정부에서 논의됐지만 설립되지 않은 전담 이민청은 교육 및 고용 정책과 통합 정책을 조율할 수 있다. 혜택별 수정은 출생이 낮은 상태에서 국가가 어떻게 인력을 유지할 것인지 말할 수 없다. 명확한 기준은 출산 후 관리 줄을 공정하게 만들 수 있다. 한국이 새로운 사람들을 어떻게 편입하느냐는 다음 줄 자리를 훨씬 넘어 인구 통계학적 미래를 형성할 것이다.

editorials.title: Rebalancing support
editorials.body: Korea needs targeted family support and a long-term immigration policy Welfare policy can turn a narrow question of eligibility into a national argument about belonging. A case in point is South Korea’s debate over multicultural family support, which began with complaints about priority access to subsidized postpartum care. It now tests whether outdated rules can be corrected without casting suspicion on those they were meant to help. The trigger was an online post asking why mothers from multicultural families shared a second-priority category with women in the national merit category when booking places through Seoul’s subsidized postpartum care program. President Lee Jae Myung took up the complaint on X, arguing that welfare should reflect financial need rather than cultural background. He has also said that programs addressing language and cultural barriers should continue. A review of current rules is justified. The Ministry of Justice has asked local governments to examine support programs and related ordinances. Seoul has begun inspecting 26 programs. Other ministries have signaled reviews. The findings should be made public, including who has received each benefit and whether families in greater need have been denied access. Korea’s multicultural policies took shape in 2006, as international marriages, particularly in rural areas, brought the hardships faced by marriage migrants and their children into public view. Support later extended to childcare and housing. The original case for assistance was clear: Many families faced poverty or language barriers and struggled to settle into Korean society. Households covered by those policies now span a wider range of economic circumstances. The share of multicultural households with monthly income above 6 million won ($4,480) rose from 2.9 percent in 2015 to 10.4 percent in 2024, according to survey data. The figures do not show that most are affluent. They do show that family background alone says little about a household’s ability to pay. That distinction matters when family status itself confers priority. It is hard to defend giving a well-off household precedence over a low-income Korean family seeking the same limited service. A migrant mother, however, may have few relatives nearby to help after childbirth, a circumstance income figures cannot capture. An effective review would trace each benefit to the disadvantage it is meant to offset and test whether its eligibility rules reach the households that need it. Where poverty is the concern, income and assets should matter more than family category. Where language barriers are at issue, tailored services may remain justified. That scrutiny should remain directed at the policies themselves. Immigrants as a group should not be made answerable for flaws in individual programs. A survey cited in the debate found that 13 percent of multicultural families had experienced discrimination. Their net enrollment rate in higher education was 61.9 percent, 13 percentage points below the national average. Criticism of poorly designed benefits can become a pretext for disparaging people who still face substantial obstacles. The definition of a multicultural family also leaves some immigrant households outside the framework. Programs largely focus on households formed by a Korean national and a foreign spouse, excluding families in which both parents are foreign nationals. Foreign workers, too, are part of Korea’s response to a shrinking workforce. Policy built around one family category cannot serve as an immigration strategy. The national population strategy released last month gave little attention to multicultural households and foreign workers. A dedicated immigration agency, discussed under the previous administration but never established, could coordinate integration policy with education and employment policy. Benefit-by-benefit revisions cannot tell the country how it will sustain its workforce, as births remain low. Clear criteria can make a postpartum-care queue fair. How Korea incorporates newcomers will shape its demographic future, far beyond the next place in line. The government belatedly took action, revealing a lack of security awareness.
Concerns are mounting over the reality that even the nation's top leader's information has been carelessly left unprotected.
editorial.bodyTr: An unprecedented incident has occurred in which personal information belonging to the president and senior government officials has been leaked outside. Files containing birth dates and passport numbers have been posted on online sites since June, yet the government stood idle before belatedly moving to contain the situation.
